title: Operator Task Framework: on-call scripting DSL & run-execution harness
creator: Marco Hernandez
description: Problem: our on-call and support teams rely on ad-hoc scripts, individual runbooks, and manual sequences that are brittle, hard to review, and difficult to audit across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments. This ticket scopes a small-footprint Operator Task Framework (OTF): a lightweight tasks-as-code DSL and a run-execution harness that turns runbooks into idempotent, testable tasks with safe parameterization, dry-run, and built-in telemetry for Redwood Console. Goals: 1) Define a compact YAML/JSON task DSL for common admin ops (rollbacks, restart pods, clear cache keys, route traffic) with explicit pre/post checks and compensating actions. 2) Implement an execution harness (Go service + CLI shim) that runs tasks as ephemeral jobs (K8s job or lambda) with strict secrets isolation, dry-run and audit log hooks. 3) Integrate with existing opsctl/helix playbooks and Console so on-call can kick off tasks, view live step logs, and automatically emit action telemetry for cost/latency/authorization traces. 4) Provide a small library of vetted tasks (rotate key, flush prefix cache, promote model variant) and a sandbox for QA. Out of scope: full runbook orchestration engine and complex workflows (defer to Runbook Orchestrator project).
acceptance_criteria: 1) DSL RFC accepted by ENG + SRE + Security. 2) Execution harness prototype runs >90% of core task types in secure sandbox with dry-run and audit-log emission to Console. 3) On-call run of 3 vetted tasks (restart backend, flush model cache prefix, failover to backup-region) completed end-to-end in staging with observability links in the Console dashboard. 4) A basic permissions mapping integrated with SSO groups (read/execute). 5) Documentation and 2 example tasks added to ops library.
progress_updates: 2026-03-08 Marco Hernandez: Created ticket and initial scope after on-call rotation retrospective. Noted repeated pain points: manual secret exposure in scripts and lack of live step telemetry.
2026-03-09 Jenna Liu: Drafted DSL proposal (minimal verbs: run_cmd, k8s_restart, http_call, kv_flush, promote_variant). Pushed proposal to /confluence/ops/otf-rfc. Requested SRE review.
2026-03-10 Aisha Patel (SRE): Raised concern about rate-limited admin APIs and suggested a circuit-breaker primitive in the DSL. Added acceptance test for idempotency.

2026-03-11 Security Review (K. Oduro): Reviewed secret handling. Mandate: no inline secrets; all parameters must be resolved from KMS-backed references. Security flagged the need for HSM integration for Private deployments.

2026-03-12 Jenna Liu: Prototype harness implemented (Go) with dry-run mode and step-level logs stored in S3. Manual test: k8s_restart task executed in staging cluster; logs linked to Console trace id: console-trace-20260312-01.

2026-03-13 Marco Hernandez: Integration spike with opsctl: added opsctl run-task --task-file support and a minimal UI button in Console to kick off sandbox tasks. Observability: events emitted to telemetry topic ops.tasks.event.

2026-03-14 QA: Running acceptance tests for cache-flush and promote-variant tasks. Found race condition when two promote-variant tasks run concurrently; mitigation: optimistic locking via model artifact version check added to DSL semantics.
notes_for_review: Key trade-offs: keep DSL intentionally small to reduce review surface; prefer harness-level primitives (circuit-breaker, concurrency limits) instead of complex language features. For Private deployments we must support KMS/HSM parameter resolution and allow audit export to customer audit stores. Need design sign-off from SRE + Security before merging to main.
next_steps: 1) Finalize RFC after SRE feedback (due 2026-03-16). 2) Harden secret resolution and HSM integration spike (Jenna). 3) Add optimistic-locking test and run concurrency fuzz tests. 4) Demo to on-call team and collect runbook translations into the DSL. 5) Prepare follow-up tickets to broaden task library.
customer_facing_summary: Internal: a safer, auditable way for on-call and support to run common admin tasks as reviewed, idempotent, and observable operations. This reduces manual errors and provides traceability for enterprise audits.
